rules.title: Type equality is interned-UID identity
rules.statement: types_equal(a,b) holds iff a and b are interned in the same type pool and share the same type-UID. Distinct UIDs are never equal even when structurally similar (e.g. Vec<i32> vs Vec<_>, two same-signature FnItems). Null on either side is unequal.

rules.title: Type equality implies compatibility
rules.statement: types_compatible(from,to) holds whenever types_equal(from,to); compatibility is the reflexive superset of equality augmented with the directed coercions below. Null on either side ⇒ incompatible.

rules.title: FnItem coerces to FnPtr of matching signature
rules.statement: A FnItem (the zero-size identity type of a named fn) coerces to a FnPtr iff arity matches and every parameter and the return type are element-wise compatible. The reverse FnPtr→FnItem is rejected, and two DIFFERENT FnItems with identical signatures are NOT compatible (they do not collapse).
rules.divergence: A6/logos-core 1.4: FnItem vs FnPtr split is a Logos addition; FnItem→FnPtr decay mirrors Rust fn-item→fn-pointer coercion.

rules.title: Never (!) coerces to every type, one direction only
rules.statement: from = Never (!) is compatible with any target type T (Never <: T). The reverse T → Never is NOT accepted.

rules.title: Inferred-type placeholder unifies either direction
rules.statement: If either from or to has kind InferredType (`_`), the pair is compatible; concrete resolution is deferred to the surrounding annotation/RHS unifier.

rules.title: Same-name struct compatibility is element-wise over type args
rules.statement: Two Struct types with equal struct_name and equal pkg_name and equal type-arg arity are compatible iff each pair of corresponding type-args is compatible (allowing inference holes, e.g. Vec<i32> ~ Vec<_>).

rules.title: Same-name enum compatibility: exact concrete scalar args, no by-value widening
rules.statement: Two Enum types with equal enum_name and pkg_name and equal nonzero type-arg arity are compatible iff for each arg pair: an unresolved arg (TypeVar/InferredType/CfgSlotType/Error) on either side unifies freely; two concrete scalars (concrete integer ≠ IntLit ≠ Enum, or F32/F64/Bool/Char) must have EXACTLY the same kind (no widening); otherwise the pair must be types_compatible.

rules.title: Integer literal coerces to any integer, TypeVar, or float
rules.statement: An IntLit is compatible with any integer-kind target, with a TypeVar, and with F32/F64. A FloatLit is compatible with F32/F64 and TypeVar.

rules.title: Cfg-slot type behaves as numeric placeholder bidirectionally
rules.statement: A CfgSlotType (deferred WritStatic-bound primitive placeholder) is compatible bidirectionally with any integer kind and with IntLit/FloatLit/F32/F64; the resolved-type compatibility is enforced later at monomorphization.

rules.title: C-style enum coerces to integer (discriminant) but never to another enum
rules.statement: An Enum from-type coerces to an integer-kind target that is itself not an Enum. Implicit integer→enum is NOT permitted (requires explicit cast / variant), and enum→enum via this rule is excluded to prevent reinterpreting incompatible layouts.

rules.title: Value-preserving integer widening is implicit
rules.statement: A concrete integer from-type coerces implicitly to a wider integer target when value preservation is guaranteed (e.g. u32→i64, i32→i64, u8→u32); signed→unsigned widening is never accepted.

rules.title: Array decays to pointer to element
rules.statement: An Array [T;N] coerces to a raw Ptr *T iff the element type equals the pointee. Additionally &[T;N] / &mut [T;N] decay to *const T/*mut T (and to &T/&mut T) with compatible element pointee, never widening mutability (shared ref only decays to const/shared element pointer).

rules.title: Array compatibility: equal size, compatible elements
rules.statement: Two Array types are compatible iff they have equal arr_size and their element types are compatible (recursively, handling nested arrays).

rules.title: Slice compatibility: no shared→mut widening, exact concrete scalar elements
rules.statement: Two Slice types are compatible iff: a shared (&[T]) slice never coerces to a mutable (&mut[T]) slice; and for elements, two concrete scalars (concrete integer ≠ IntLit ≠ Enum, or F32/F64/Bool/Char) must match exactly (slices alias raw memory, so no stride-changing widening), while inference holes unify via types_compatible.

rules.title: Tuple compatibility is element-wise
rules.statement: Two Tuple types are compatible iff they have equal arity and each pair of corresponding element types is compatible.

rules.title: &Closure / &mut Closure coerce to Closure
rules.statement: A Ref or MutRef whose pointee is a Closure coerces to a bare Closure target (a `dyn FnMut(..)` annotation parses to Closure, so `take_ref(&cl)` type-checks against `f: &dyn FnMut(..)`).

rules.title: Struct and references to struct coerce to &dyn Trait
rules.statement: A TraitObject target accepts a from-type that is a Struct, a Ptr to anything, or a Ref/MutRef whose pointee is a Struct; the actual trait-impl satisfaction is checked at codegen.

rules.title: Reference/pointer coercions follow permission lattice over compatible pointees
rules.statement: &T↔*const T, &mut T↔*mut T (and *T→&T reverse) coerce when pointees are compatible; &mut T→&T (exclusive→shared) is allowed; *mut T→*const T (drop write) is allowed; &T→&T and &mut T→&mut T propagate over compatible pointees. Mutability is only ever dropped, never gained.

rules.title: &Vec<T> / &mut Vec<T> coerce to &[T]
rules.statement: A Ref/MutRef whose pointee is the stdlib struct Vec<T> coerces to a Slice whose element is compatible with Vec's first type-arg (Vec's {ptr,len,cap} layout has the {ptr,len} slice fat-pointer as a prefix). Hardcoded to the stdlib Vec; general Deref is not yet covered.
rules.uncertainty: Hardcoded special-case for struct named "Vec"; not a general Deref-trait rule.

rules.title: Raw pointer coerces to a tagged trait pointer
rules.statement: Any raw Ptr coerces to a TaggedPtr target (&tagged<TS> Trait is a thin pointer to a tagged object; the tag is read at dispatch time).

rules.title: Concrete struct symbol name = base + module suffix + generic args
rules.statement: A Struct/ZonedStruct type's symbol name is its struct_name, plus a module-qualification suffix `$M<module_id>` for non-stdlib packages with a known owning module (stdlib `logos.*` and empty-map compiles get no suffix), plus, when type_args are present, `$G<n>` followed by `$`-joined per-arg mangled type names.

rules.title: Per-type mangling for generic-symbol identity
rules.statement: Each type mangles to an identity-stable string: Ptr→pmut_/pcst_+pointee; Ref→ref_; MutRef→refmut_; Array→arr<N>_elem; Tuple→tup$<n>$..; Slice→slice_/UnsizedSlice→uslice_; UnsizedDyn→udyn_<trait>; DstRef→dst[mut]ref_<name>; AssocType→base::name; WStaticLit→hs_<hex64 of const value> (identical bytes ⇒ same suffix); owning TraitObject→owndyn_<trait>+args distinct from borrowed &dyn; struct/enum module-qualified. Two structurally distinct generic instantiations get distinct symbols.

rules.title: Owning Box<dyn T> and borrowed &dyn T mangle distinctly
rules.statement: An owning trait object mangles to `owndyn_<trait>` plus its type-args, distinct from a borrowed &dyn T (which keeps the type_str mangling), so e.g. Vec<Box<dyn T>> and Vec<&dyn T> are distinct generic struct specs (preserving owning-ness for drop).

rules.title: Same pkg::Type from two modules coexist via module-id suffix
rules.statement: Every type-keyed symbol embeds the type's owning module_id as `$M<id>` so two separately-compiled modules each declaring the same pkg::Type do not collide at link. stdlib packages (`logos.*`) are globally unique and never qualified; an empty pkg→module map yields no suffix (byte-identical output for non-module compiles).
rules.divergence: A6: full type-coexistence is a Logos module-model addition.

rules.title: Function signature key = base + per-param mangled types
rules.statement: A function's signature key is `<base>__<mangled param type>...`, with `__void` appended when there are no params and `__vararg` when variadic. For a fn-ptr-impl method (base begins `$fnptr$`), fn-pointer parameters are erased to their arity-only `$fnptr$<n>` form so the symbol is stable across the impl's type-vars.

rules.title: Function link symbol embeds module/package; extern and methods carve-outs
rules.statement: A function's link symbol is mangled from {module_id, package, base, signature, is_generic, is_method, is_extern}; two packages defining the same base+signature fn get distinct symbols. Extern fns keep their bare ABI C name; struct methods (base contains `__`) are disambiguated via their struct's pkg-qualified name.

rules.title: Call candidate set filtered by package visibility and imports
rules.statement: Function-call candidates for a base name are restricted to fns whose package is empty (extern/prelude), equals the current package, or appears in the current wildcard imports; a `use pkg from <module>` import excludes fns from other modules of that package. An explicit `pkg::fn` qualifier restricts to exactly that package with no empty-fallback (a miss is a genuine error). When non-qualified filtering would leave nothing and the emptiness is not an intentional `from`-restriction, all candidates are returned (robustness for synthetic phases).

rules.title: Generic-overload selection prefers current package and matching arity
rules.statement: Among generic overloads of a base name, only candidates passing the package-qualifier visibility check are considered; arity must match (≥ param count for vararg, exact otherwise). A candidate in the current package wins immediately; otherwise the first arity-matching candidate is chosen, with an arity-mismatched candidate kept only as last-resort fallback.

rules.title: Exact-signature lookup admits FnItem→FnPtr argument coercion
rules.statement: find_func_by_base_and_signature matches a candidate when arity and vararg-ness agree and every parameter is types_equal, EXCEPT a FnItem argument matches an FnPtr parameter when their signatures are types_compatible (so a bare fn-name argument matches a `f: fn() -> R` parameter).

rules.title: Non-generic call resolution scores exact > compatible, errors on ambiguity
rules.statement: Among arity-matching non-generic candidates, each argument scores 2 if types_equal to the parameter else 1 if types_compatible (unless exact_only) else rejects the candidate; the candidate with the highest minimum-of-argument score wins. A tie is ambiguous and is broken by preferring a candidate whose package equals the current package (local shadows imported); an unresolved tie is a compile error "ambiguous call to '<name>'".

rules.title: A call diverges iff callee is `panic` or returns Never
rules.statement: A CALL or FN_MACRO_CALL node is divergent (control never returns past it) iff the callee is the macro `panic` or any candidate fn for the callee has return type Never (!). Marker macros unreachable!/todo!/unimplemented! lower through panic! and are handled via the panic fast-path.
